solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: to wall something is to enclose it, so one word surrounds the other here

parts.note: to fend is to provide, as in fend for yourself
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church is protected because someone pays for walls to be built around it.
explanation.walkthrough: The church sits inside FEND: FEN-CE-D.
explanation.definitionFit: A fenced area is enclosed by barriers, so it is guarded or kept safe.

clue.text: Old enough to be a model

parts.note: ex- means former
ample means plenty, sufficient

explanation.surface: Someone has reached the age at which they may work as a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a model to follow, as in setting an example.

clue.text: Bridge over single channel in US state

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part sitting over another simply comes before it in the column

parts.note: a bridge links two sides
I is the Roman numeral one
a cut is a canal or channel

explanation.surface: Somewhere in America a bridge spans a single waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: Connecticut is one of the New England states of the USA.

indicators.note: the second reckless describes careless, uncontrolled handling of the following word, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
rate is speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A repetitive warning about dangerous driving, like a road sign shouting the same words twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated phrase does three jobs: the first word is the definition, the second jumbles the first speed, and the last speed is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate acts are rash and heedless of risk, so desperate can mean reckless.

parts.note: butch means manly, so butcher is the comparative
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father tells his son to appear more masculine.
explanation.walkthrough: Have a butcher's is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook rhymes with look.
explanation.definitionFit: In British rhyming slang a butcher's is a quick glance, from butcher's hook standing for look.

clue.text: Weapon that can't be fired point-blank?

definitions.text: Weapon that can't be fired point-blank?

parts.words: Weapon that can't be fired point-blank
parts.note: surface reading: a gun that is unsafe to discharge at close range
setter's reading: a weapon with no point, which nobody fires at all, such as a cosh

explanation.walkthrough: Point-blank sounds like close range; read it as lacking a point, and the weapon is one you hit with rather than shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunt instrument is a heavy object without an edge used to strike someone, a staple of murder reports.

clue.text: No change of scenery over in Italian city

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned over means flipped so it runs upward

parts.note: being in a rut means the same dull routine with nothing new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller complains of seeing the same landscape while visiting Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is the major city of Piedmont in northern Italy, home of Fiat.

clue.text: Every second of the day I'm clumsy

indicators.note: asks for the second letter of each of the following words in turn

parts.note: second letter of this word
second letter of this word
second letter, skipping the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being awkward every moment of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: I'm is both the source of the last letter and, in the surface, the subject of clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ham is used for clumsy, as in ham-fisted or a ham actor's crude performance.

clue.text: Reboot primarily due to a faulty data display

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter

indicators.note: something faulty is broken and not in working order, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A computer had to be restarted because of a fault in the hardware.
explanation.definitionFit: A readout is information shown on a screen or dial by an instrument or computer.

clue.text: Empty vehicle that one's broken into

indicators.note: a thing that has been broken into has an intruder now sitting inside it

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A van was burgled and found to have nothing left in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain can mean empty or hollow, as in vain promises or a vain hope.

parts.note: surface reading: a filling, hearty dinner
setter's reading: a meal whose shape is the opposite of round

explanation.walkthrough: Not round here sounds like a remark that such food is unavailable locally; it actually says the meal is the shape that is not round.
explanation.definitionFit: A square meal is a substantial, nourishing one that leaves you full.

clue.text: A lot of interest paid on plastic

indicators.note: plastic material can be moulded into any shape, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about the large interest charges on their credit card.
explanation.walkthrough: A lot seems to mean a large amount; it is the definition, lot in the sense of one's fate. Plastic is slang for a credit card.
explanation.definitionFit: Your lot is your fortune in life, and predestination is a fate fixed in advance.

parts.note: surface reading: a cabaret singer of easy-listening songs
setter's reading: a portable lamp, so a singer associated with that kind of light

explanation.walkthrough: Light entertainment suggests frothy variety shows; the light is a flashlight.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch singer performs sentimental songs of unrequited love, carrying a torch for someone.

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
to strain is to pass through a sieve

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect a filter and run something through it a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back, the same as to restrain it.

clue.text: Find fish on banks of river with it

indicators.note: something on both banks lies either side, enclosing what flows between

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish
R is the abbreviation for river
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler is told where fish can be found along a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: Find looks like a verb but is the noun, a valuable discovery.
explanation.definitionFit: A find is something uncommon and valuable that has been discovered, which is a rarity.

clue.text: Very good gathering at home making friends again

indicators.note: gathering means drawing in alongside, so one short piece is attached to the end of another

parts.note: really means very, as in really good
in means at home
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A very good party held at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the definition as re-allying, joining again as allies.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-ally is to form an alliance once more, so reallying is becoming friends again.

parts.note: in means fashionable, as is chic

indicators.note: a vacated building has been emptied out, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Chewing gum has been left behind in an empty lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicle is the natural gum from the sapodilla tree, the traditional base of chewing gum.

definitions.note: used adjectivally, as in a hairpin bend
definitions.meaning: first meaning: as sharp as a U-shaped bend in a road
second meaning: a pin holding the hair in place

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single phrase about holding on hard; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpin bend doubles back sharply, and a hairpin is also a hair grip.

indicators.note: to lock something in is to shut it inside, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to try is to test
to pine for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: A suggestion to test the locks fitted to a wooden pine box.
explanation.walkthrough: Pine looks like the wood of the box but is the verb, to long.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a large light wooden crate, once used to ship tea and now for moving house.

clue.text: Topless, for a gesture, first lady

indicators.note: without its top, a word in a down entry loses its opening letter
says which piece goes at the front of the assembled word

parts.note: a sign is a gesture
taken as written, then beheaded
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gesture is made towards a first lady who appears topless.
explanation.definitionFit: Signora is the Italian title for a married woman, the equivalent of Mrs or lady.

parts.note: surface reading: a protected historic structure
setter's reading: a tower that leans, and to list is to lean

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: the Leaning Tower of Pisa lists. In Britain a protected historic building is officially listed.
explanation.definitionFit: A listed building is one on the official UK register of protected historic structures.

parts.note: D stood for the old British penny, a copper coin
to rake is to comb through

explanation.surface: A famous explorer's possessions include an antique copper comb.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is. Before 1971 a British penny was written d.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan seafarer who circumnavigated the globe.

clue.text: Fix pockets for a coat with one type of wax

indicators.note: to pocket something is to take it inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: to set is to fix
per means for each, as in ten pounds per item
a mac is a raincoat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Instructions for sewing pockets onto a coat waterproofed with wax.
explanation.definitionFit: Spermaceti is the waxy substance from a sperm whale's head, once used for candles.

indicators.note: something caught by the next words is trapped among their letters

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A badger is trapped by a hunter for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: Badger looks like the animal but is the verb, to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To rag someone is to tease or torment them, the same as to badger.

indicators.note: says that the letter for left is swapped for the letter for right

parts.note: a glow is a soft light

explanation.surface: Instructions for making a beam of light travel from one side to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: Left to right sounds like a direction of travel; it means L changes to R.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow crops or vegetables is to produce them.

indicators.note: to nurse is to cradle and hold close, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: to intimate is to hint or suggest
'n' is a shortened and, as in rock 'n' roll

explanation.surface: Nurses described as the cosiest and closest of colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: And looks like a link joining two adjectives; it is the letter N inside the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug means warm and cosy, so the superlative is the warmest.

parts.note: a germ is a bud or sprout
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: An order to open fire on someone from northern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A German is a person from Germany, a country in central Europe.
